newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-US T-bonds seen defying overbought signals.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-US T-bonds seen defying overbought signals.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond futures are likely to maintain a positive bias in the near term despite overbought signals in daily oscillator charts that have persisted in recent weeks, technical analysts said.
Minor pullbacks and sideways consolidation in the past week have done little to resolve the market's overbought condition, but that reflects the strength of the uptrend, they noted.
"We have been heavily overbought since very close to the beginning of the month," said Eric Wall, a senior technical analyst at MMS International.
"It did appear that a little bearish divergence was going to emerge earlier in the month, but that really didn't pan out and the market continued to rally," he added.

Wall said overbought signals on the daily stochastic were followed by a downturn 65 to 70 percent of the time but were not a good actual sell signal because of big potential losses that would be incurred by huge impulsive rallies that sometimes overran them.
"When the market is strong, it will be overbought," agreed Matthew Crosson, director of fixed income at Pegasus Econometrics Group.

Analysts said a trend should be respected when it defies oscillators. They pointed out that the market had not penetrated any significant support levels lately and bearish readings on the candlestick charts have also proven false.

"I still see the market in an accelerating channel bound from 113-9/32 on the high end of it to 111-15/32," Crosson said. Analysts added that 113-9/32 was also a major intermediate-term top for September T-bond futures marked on February 18, making it an obvious target for now.
Septembers were off 5/32 on the day at 112-12/32 in late morning trade after bouncing from an early low of 112-8/32.

"We had a pretty good retreat from the highs on Friday, and we're just seeing a little profit-taking," Wall said. "This has in no way disturbed our positive view. People can probably look for bid to re-emerge as the day goes on."
He added that the weekly stochastic was edging up steadily without running into overbought territory yet.
"So there's still plenty of room for further upside development," he said.
Beyond the widely watched 113-9/32 resistance, Wall said a trendline from the January 1996 high came in at 113-23/32 on the weekly continuous chart.
With the Federal Open Market Committee scheduled to meet July 1-2, the market was likely to be very cautious this week, analysts said.
Wall noted that Fed funds futures did not appear to have priced in any interest-rate change so far.
In Eurodollar futures, he said the December contract was eyeing a trendline from last December's highs, currently coming in at around 94.00.
The positive longer-term view would remain in place until the 93.775 mid-May high is broken, and day-traders should look at dips toward 93.915 as a buying opportunity, he said.
